summary.en: In the late 1950s, good-looking, non-threatening teen idols surge and win big commercially.
summary.zh: 50年代末，长相俊秀且没有危险性的青少年偶像涌现，在商业上取得了巨大成功。

body.zh:
50年代末，长相俊秀且没有危险性的青少年偶像涌现，在商业上取得了巨大成功。

现在该开始谈谈青少年偶像了。在我的书里，将之翻译成受无所事事年轻人推崇的青年偶像。从音乐产业上来讲，打造青少年偶像之举颇有逐利之意，比如只展现Elvis Presley的魅力，而剔除所有危险性因素，使其成为少女、孩童以及青少年眼中，一位绝无非分之想的理想男友。这样的人能令年轻女孩们端坐庭前，倾听着仿佛只为她们而唱的歌，就像他会牵起她们的手，甚至亲吻脸颊，并要深入了解她们。所以，这类理想男友形象瞄准的是少女市场。

关于青少年偶像很重要的一点是，外表要特别帅，还要唱得凑合。当然，如果唱功不佳，可以在录音室修音，但他们一定要看起来帅。比起凭借能力出人头地的顶尖音乐家，他们更像是时尚模特，其次才考虑他们的嗓音和音乐。这些青少年偶像更像是按照Pat Boone这种清秀形象为原型打造出来的，而不是Elvis Presley。如果你关注Elvis的职业生涯，他在1958年开始服兵役，1960年退伍，公司也曾经试图打造主流的Elvis形象，从60年代早期到中期这段时间，Elvis在好莱坞参与了各类电影的拍摄。话说回来，Elvis甚至有往青少年偶像的方向发展过，比如1960年的冠军单曲《Are You Lonesome Tonight》，其来源可追溯到1920年代。Elvis的版本是第一首加入独白的，它不仅是首慢歌，还会在歌中听到他读了几行莎士比亚风格的诗句。就像他正对着一个年轻女子倾声耳语。这绝对是Elvis的一张青少年偶像唱片，可谓生而逢时。在1960年，他就有放下摇滚乐，转向主流听众的倾向。

当时也有其他的青年偶像风靡一时，其中的确也有实力派，比如Frankie Avalon，以及稍后我会提到的Fabian，他们都是来自费城，由Bob Marcucci担任经纪人，隶属于Chancellor Records。Bob Marcucci创作歌曲，制作唱片，拥有这家公司，他很像我们稍后要讲的Phil Spector。他旗下栽培了很多青少年偶像。Frankie Avalon的冠军单曲包括1959年的《Venus》 和《Why》。不过进入60年代后，作为青少年偶像的Frankie Avalon不仅在榜单上占有一席之地，更是开始与Annette Funicello搭档演艺。Annette在演电影之前，曾是一度流行的电视节目 《Mickey Mouse Club (米老鼠俱乐部)》中的演员。Frankie与Annette合作的Beach Party（海滩聚会）系列电影，例如《Beach Blanket Bingo》，成为了年轻人喜爱的娱乐形式，是专为青少年打造的。Bob Marcucci旗下的另一名费城小伙Fabian，1959年发行了《Turn Me Loose》、《Tiger》等。Fabian可能在演唱技巧、能力或天资方面略逊一筹，但至少他长得帅。

还有来自北达科他州的Bobby Vee，1961年在洛杉矶的Liberty Records录制了一首冠军单曲《Take Good Care of My Baby》，歌曲的创作者是Gerry Goffin与Carole King。Bobby Vinton隶属于纽约的Epic，Epic是Columbia Records的一个子公司。Bobby在1962年有一首非常成功的冠军单曲《Roses Are Red (My Love)》，还有一系列热单。然后是Bobby Darin，分别在58和59年拥有《Splish Splash》和《Dream Lover》这些热单。他有一首金曲1959年的《Mack the Knife》，实际上是出自一部叫做《The Three Penny Opera》的Kurt Weill歌剧，这算是一种古典乐至少是歌剧与摇滚乐的crossover。

这就是关于青少年偶像的大致印象：理想的男友形象，可能是为了牟取私利而精心包装的产品。你可以一笑置之，但这些人的唱片销量确是很可观，从音乐行业的视角来看，这种包装是当时极为成功的战略。
body.en:
In the late 1950s, good-looking, non-threatening teen idols surge and win big commercially.

Time for teen idols. In my book I render the idea as youth idols for idle young listeners. Industry-wise the move is profit-minded: keep Elvis’s charm, strip the danger, and sell an ideal boyfriend who would never cross a line—someone a girl can sit and hear as if he sang only for her, might take her hand, kiss a cheek, want to know her. The target is the girl market.

Looks come first; singing only has to be good enough. Studio fixes can cover weak vocals; they must look handsome. They are closer to fashion models than to top musicians who rise on craft. The template is closer to Pat Boone’s clean face than to Elvis. Follow Elvis’s career: he enters the army in 1958, returns in 1960; the company pushes a mainstream image, and through the early–mid 1960s he shoots Hollywood films. He even tilts teen-idol: 1960’s No. 1 “Are You Lonesome Tonight?” reaches back to the 1920s. His cut is the first with a spoken monologue—a slow song plus Shakespearean-flavored lines whispered toward a young woman. Pure teen-idol Elvis, well timed. By 1960 he already leans away from rock toward mainstream listeners.

Other idols boom; some have real chops. Frankie Avalon and, later, Fabian come from Philadelphia under Bob Marcucci at Chancellor Records. Marcucci writes, produces, owns the label—somewhat like Phil Spector later. Avalon’s No. 1s include 1959’s “Venus” and “Why.” Into the 1960s he stays on the charts and pairs with Annette Funicello (ex–Mickey Mouse Club) in Beach Party films such as Beach Blanket Bingo—teen entertainment built for teens. Marcucci’s other Philly kid Fabian cuts 1959’s “Turn Me Loose” and “Tiger”; weaker on voice or gift, but he looks the part.

Bobby Vee from North Dakota hits No. 1 in 1961 on Liberty in L.A. with Goffin/King’s “Take Good Care of My Baby.” Bobby Vinton is on Epic (a Columbia subsidiary) in New York; 1962’s “Roses Are Red (My Love)” is a major No. 1 among other hits. Bobby Darin has 1958’s “Splish Splash” and 1959’s “Dream Lover,” plus 1959’s “Mack the Knife” from Kurt Weill’s The Threepenny Opera—a classical/opera crossover into the rock world.

That is the teen-idol sketch: ideal boyfriend, often a packaged product. You can laugh; sales are real. From the industry’s view the packaging is a highly successful strategy.
